s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea with exertional and orthopneic components, fatigue, dry cough, and lower limb swelling, suggesting a chronic cardiopulmonary condition with possible systemic involvement
salient_findings: Bilateral lower limb swelling worse in evenings
Pulmonary edema on CT angiography chest
key_facts: 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement
Interstitial lung disease four years prior
Vital signs: BP 138/86 mmHg, pulse 85/min, temperature 96.5°F (35.8°C), BMI 16.3 kg/m², respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 93% on 3L oxygen
Bilateral ulnar deviation at metacarpophalangeal joints with swan neck deformities
Left ventricular ejection fraction 45-50% on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Chronic heart failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and fatigue, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45-50% on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Interstitial lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of interstitial lung disease and current symptoms of dyspnea and dry cough

shortlist.label: Pulmonary hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of dyspnea and fatigue, with a history of interstitial lung disease and possible systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated lung disease

raw.rationale: The patient has a 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement, complicated by interstitial lung disease, and high rheumatoid factor levels, which suggests rheumatoid arthritis. The presence of interstitial lung disease and the patient's symptoms such as dyspnea on exertion and dry cough also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic heart failure
rejected.why: Although the patient has symptoms such as dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower limb swelling, the left ventricular ejection fraction is 45-50%, which is not severely reduced, and there is no significant jugular venous distention or increased work of breathing.

rejected.label: Interstitial lung disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of interstitial lung disease, the current symptoms and findings suggest a more complex condition involving the lungs and joints.

rejected.label: Pulmonary hypertension
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of pulmonary hypertension, such as elevated pulmonary artery pressures or right ventricular dysfunction.

rejected.label: Constrictive pericarditis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of pericardial disease or constriction, such as pericardial effusion or calcification, and the patient's symptoms and findings do not suggest this condition.
